about.bio:
Hi! I'm Pip - a product designer. I've been in tech since 2018.

At Ultraleap I led an interaction R&D team - proving the value of high fidelity hand tracking. I'm now at FitXR, designing fitness apps for people who hate fitness, across xr and mobile.

I combine simplicity and fun to create experiences that feel joyful and inevitable.

work.description: FitXR is a leading VR fitness app that transforms home workouts through immersive, gamified training.

caseStudies.title: Early User Experience
caseStudies.imageAlt: Early user experience case study image
caseStudies.description: Hitting key metrics through user centred design. +16% new user conversion, +10% paywall conversion, +30% users playing one or more classes - all by caring + addressing user needs.

caseStudies.title: Sidestep, Jump & Crouch
caseStudies.imageAlt: Sidestep jump crouch case study image
caseStudies.description: Spatial interaction design for a mass market VR fitness application. Prototyped, tested & shipped 3 new moves for FitXR in 3 months. Elicited user responses like "FINALLY, my pulse was RACING. LOVE IT."

work.description: Ultraleap was a spatial interaction company that enabled natural interaction through world-leading hand tracking and mid-air, ultrasonic haptics.

caseStudies.title: Hyperion Showcase
caseStudies.tags: Flagship demos which led to OEM opportunities
caseStudies.description: Novel XR interaction research + design to create flagship demos, opening up new business opportunities for Ultraleap.

caseStudies.title: Interaction Archive
caseStudies.description: At Ultraleap, I designed and contributed to a lot of different interactions and apps! I've archived all of them here.

caseStudies.title: XR Design Guidelines
caseStudies.description: I helped write & rework Ultraleap's XR Guidelines - providing guidance and insight into our best recommendations for XR Hand Tracking interactions.

caseStudies.title: Dog Racer
caseStudies.tags: Leading a team through a tough project
caseStudies.description: Building a launch application for Leap2 in just four weeks, leading a team that wasn't happy about it.
